title: Kingdom of Holland
capsule: The Kingdom of Holland (1806–1810) was a French satellite monarchy carved from the Batavian Republic and placed under Napoleon's brother Louis Bonaparte. Louis I proved an unexpectedly conscientious ruler — he learned Dutch, resisted enforcing the Continental System, refused to levy full conscription, and founded institutions that became the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences and the precursor to the Rijksmuseum. His conflicts with Napoleon over these policies led Napoleon to order French troops to occupy Amsterdam in July 1810; Louis abdicated on 1 July and the kingdom was formally annexed to France as a group of departments on 9 July 1810.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well attested; the kingdom's borders are documented in French imperial administrative records and the Treaty of Campoformio framework, though the exact inclusion of East Frisian districts fluctuated year to year.
